title: Weighted Average Purchase Price Per Product
description:
Calculate the quantity-weighted average unit price for each product across multiple purchase orders at different prices.

**Table: purchase_orders** — `id`, `product_id`, `product_name`, `quantity`, `unit_price`

Output columns: `product_name`, `total_qty`, `weighted_avg_price`. Order by `product_name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE purchase_orders (id INT, product_id INT, product_name VARCHAR, quantity INT, unit_price DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO purchase_orders VALUES (1,1,'Widget A',100,5.00),(2,1,'Widget A',50,5.50),(3,1,'Widget A',150,4.80),(4,2,'Gadget B',30,25.00),(5,2,'Gadget B',70,24.00),(6,3,'Book C',200,12.00),(7,3,'Book C',100,12.50),(8,4,'Shirt D',60,18.00),(9,4,'Shirt D',40,19.00);
solution_sql: SELECT product_name, SUM(quantity) AS total_qty, ROUND(SUM(quantity * unit_price) / SUM(quantity), 2) AS weighted_avg_price FROM purchase_orders GROUP BY product_id, product_name ORDER BY product_name

test_cases.description: 4 products; Widget A had 3 purchases at different prices; weighted avg reflects quantity mix

hints: Weighted average = SUM(quantity * unit_price) / SUM(quantity) — multiply each price by its weight (quantity) before averaging.
A plain AVG(unit_price) would be wrong here because it ignores the different quantities purchased at each price.
explanation: Simple average treats all prices equally regardless of volume. Weighted average accounts for how much was bought at each price. Widget A: (100×5.00 + 50×5.50 + 150×4.80) / 300 = 1495/300 = 4.98. Gadget B: (30×25 + 70×24) / 100 = 2430/100 = 24.30. Book C: (200×12 + 100×12.50) / 300 = 12.17. Shirt D: (60×18 + 40×19) / 100 = 18.40.
